title: Exposure may exceed an Atlas maximum by up to 5% only when the excess is accrued interest
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.1.7 states that where the Atlas specifies a maximum exposure, "actual exposure may exceed that maximum by up to 5%, provided the excess is solely attributable to accrued interest and not to new principal."

The carve-out is narrow by construction. Interest accrues without anyone acting, so a hard cap would put a compliant Agent into technical breach purely through the passage of time. Rather than restate every limit as an approximation, the Atlas grants a bounded tolerance and then attaches the origin test: only accrual qualifies, and any excess traceable to a new allocation decision is a real breach at the original number.

The obligation half is what keeps the tolerance from becoming a 5% headroom allowance: "A Prime Agent is responsible for claiming and returning accrued interest as necessary to keep exposure within the specified maximum." The tolerance is a grace period for mechanical drift, not a permanent expansion of mandate — the Agent must actively work exposure back down rather than park at 105%.

The trade-off is that enforcement now depends on attributing the excess to a cause, which is harder to check than a flat threshold. Compliance becomes an accounting question rather than a balance lookup.
description: The tolerance covers unavoidable yield accrual, never new principal, and the Prime Agent must claim and return interest to pull exposure back under the stated cap.
